items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: He liked my way of playing and he asked me if I would be willing to do a duet with him at the Olympia Music Hall for three weeks in October. We would play 'Summertime' together

ctx.x: The 1st of July, 1967, we moved from Paris to Fontenay Sous Bois where we still live, because we had decided that the rent of our other flat was too high for our deflated purse! We found a very nice four roomed apartment on the sixth floor of a modern building, and we had a gorgeous view over the woods of Vincennes and even Paris.

I had met a fmous French singer named Michel Polnareff during a tour in France. He liked my way of playing and he asked me if I would be willing to do a duet with him at the Olympia Music Hall for three weeks in October. We would play 'Summertime' together, me having a few chorus on trumpet, then him, imitating the sound of a trumpet with a wa-wa. I accepted as it was good publicity to work at the Olympia and Polnareff had a big name. The number had a big success. Polnareff had a big voice for such a little…

But I had a bad souvenir of Polnareff because after the Olympia, his manager asked me if I w uld play the number again for a televised show. Lily asked what the conditions would be but we could never get a straight answer. Finally, he agreed on our terms.
